1º de Primaria · Inglés

My school

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Open your school bag. What's in it? Can you say one thing in English?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Maybe a book, a pencil or a rubber. In this unit you will learn the names of all your school things.

2

Aprende12 apartados

Para empezar: Where is my rubber?

It is Monday morning. Sam opens his school bag.

«My book… yes. My pencil… yes. My crayons… yes. My rubber… oh no! Where is my rubber?»

Sam looks under the table. He looks on the chair. No rubber!

His friend Lily smiles. «Here you are, Sam. It's on the floor.»

«Thank you, Lily!» says Sam. The teacher claps her hands. «Sit down, please. Open your books!»

Now Sam is ready to learn.

1. My school bag

This is my school bag. It is red and blue.

In my bag I have a book, a notebook and a pencil case.

Every day I take my bag to school. What colour is your school bag?

2. Pencil, rubber and ruler

In my pencil case I have a pencil, a rubber and a ruler.

I write with a pencil. I rub out mistakes with a rubber.

I draw straight lines with a ruler. In the USA, a rubber is called an eraser.

Vídeo: Do You Have A Crayon? School Supplies Song · Super Simple Songs (YouTube) · 9,9 millones de visualizaciones

3. Crayons, scissors and glue

For art, we use crayons, scissors and glue.

I colour with crayons. I cut paper with scissors. I stick paper with glue.

Be careful with scissors! Always walk, never run.

4. What's this?

To ask about a thing, we say: What's this?

We answer: It's a pencil. or It's a book.

Before a word that starts with a, e, i, o, u, we say an: It's an eraser.

5. In my classroom

Look around your classroom.

There is a board, a table and a chair for every child. There is a door and a window too.

The teacher writes on the board. We sit on our chairs.

Vídeo: School Supplies: What's in My Bag? · English Singsing (YouTube) · 9,4 millones de visualizaciones

6. Classroom instructions

The teacher says instructions. Listen and do!

Stand up! Sit down! Listen! Look!

Open your book! Close your book! Be quiet, please! Play the game and move your body.

7. Can I have…, please?

To ask for something, we say: Can I have a pencil, please?

The answer is: Here you are!

Then we say: Thank you! Being polite is important at school.

8. How many pencils?

Let's count school things.

How many pencils? One, two, three. Three pencils!

Remember: with more than one, add s. One book, two books. One crayon, five crayons.

9. My school day

At school we do many things. We read, we write and we draw.

We sing songs and we play in the playground.

At ten o'clock the bell rings. It's time to play!

10. My teacher and my friends

At school there is a teacher and many friends.

We say: This is my teacher. Her name is Ms Smith.

And: This is my friend. His name is Tom. We help each other and share.

Vídeo: School Supplies Song · English Tree (YouTube) · 13,6 millones de visualizaciones

11. Game: Kim's game

Put five school things on the table. Look carefully.

Close your eyes. Your friend takes one thing away.

Open your eyes. What's missing? Say it in English: The ruler!

12. Review: my school things

Now you can name your school things: pencil, rubber, ruler, book, bag, crayons and scissors.

You know the classroom: board, table and chair.

You can ask What's this? and Can I have…, please? Well done!

Lo hacemos juntos · Let's do it together

Your friend shows you a pencil. Ask and answer.

  1. Ask: What's this?
  2. Look at the thing.
  3. Answer: It's a…

Resultado: What's this? It's a pencil.

You need a rubber. Ask your friend.

  1. Start with: Can I have…
  2. Say the thing: a rubber.
  3. Don't forget: please!

Resultado: Can I have a rubber, please?

The teacher says «Stand up!». What do you do?

  1. Listen carefully.
  2. Stand up means levantarse.

Resultado: You stand up.

How many crayons? ✏️✏️✏️✏️

  1. Count: one, two, three, four.
  2. More than one: add s.

Resultado: Four crayons.

Errores típicos

  • Saying «a eraser»: before a, e, i, o, u we say «an eraser».
  • Forgetting the s in plurals: «two pencils», not «two pencil».
  • Saying «Give me a pencil»: it is more polite to say «Can I have a pencil, please?».
  • Mixing up «rubber» and «ruler»: a rubber rubs out, a ruler draws lines.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (22)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Point to your pencil and say: pencil.

    Ver solución
    Pencil.

  2. Show me your book.

    Ver solución
    The child shows a book.

  3. Name three things in your pencil case.

    Ver solución
    For example, pencil, rubber, ruler.

  4. Stand up! Sit down!

    Ver solución
    The child stands up and sits down.

  5. Draw a school bag and colour it.

    Ver solución
    A school bag in any colour.

  6. What do you use to cut paper?

    Ver solución
    Scissors.

  7. Match: lápiz – pencil, libro – book.

    Ver solución
    Pencil = lápiz; book = libro.

  8. Open your book! Close your book!

    Ver solución
    The child opens and closes the book.

Nivel medio

  1. Answer: What's this? (a ruler)

    Ver solución
    It's a ruler.

  2. Complete: Can I have a ____, please?

    Ver solución
    pencil / rubber / crayon (free answer).

  3. How many chairs are there at your table?

    Ver solución
    Free answer, for example: four chairs.

  4. Draw three blue crayons.

    Ver solución
    Three crayons coloured blue.

  5. What do you say when someone gives you a pencil?

    Ver solución
    Thank you!

  6. Complete: It's ___ eraser.

    Ver solución
    an.

  7. Write two things in your classroom.

    Ver solución
    For example, board, table, chair, door, window.

  8. Play «Teacher says» with a friend: give three instructions.

    Ver solución
    For example: Stand up! Listen! Sit down!

  9. Say what you do at school: We read, we…

    Ver solución
    We write, we draw, we sing, we play.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Describe your pencil case: «In my pencil case I have…».

    Ver solución
    Free answer: In my pencil case I have two pencils and a rubber.

  2. Play Kim's game with five things. What's missing?

    Ver solución
    Free answer: The ruler!

  3. Introduce your teacher: «This is my teacher. Her/His name is…».

    Ver solución
    Free answer.

  4. Ask three friends «Can I have…, please?» and write what they give you.

    Ver solución
    Free answer.

  5. Make a label for five things in your bedroom or classroom in English.

    Ver solución
    For example: table, chair, door, window, book.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeThe classroom shop

We open a small shop in our classroom. We buy and sell school things in English.

Pasos

  1. We collect school things: pencils, rubbers, rulers, crayons.
  2. We make price labels with numbers from one to ten.
  3. The shopper asks: Can I have a ruler, please? The shopkeeper says: Here you are!
  4. We change roles and say thank you and goodbye.

Producto final: A classroom shop and a short dialogue in English.

Cómo se valora

  • Names school things in English.
  • Asks politely with please and thank you.
  • Uses What's this? It's a…

Resumen visualTodo el tema en una pantalla

Glosario

Pencil
A thing to write with (lápiz).
Rubber
A thing to rub out mistakes (goma). Also eraser.
Ruler
A thing to draw straight lines (regla).
Crayon
A thing to colour with (cera).
Scissors
A thing to cut paper (tijeras).
Bag
A thing to carry your books (mochila).
Board
The big thing the teacher writes on (pizarra).
Chair
A thing to sit on (silla).
Table
A thing to work on (mesa).
Classroom
The room where we learn (clase).
6

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Al preparar la mochila, nombrad las cosas en inglés: book, pencil, rubber.
  • Jugad a «Kim's game» en casa con cinco objetos.
  • Pegad etiquetas en inglés en algunos muebles: table, chair, door.
  • Pedid las cosas en inglés durante un rato: «Can I have the salt, please?».

Para profesores

Saberes: Lengua extranjera (Inglés): léxico del aula y del material escolar; estructuras What's this? It's a/an…, Can I have…, please?; comprensión de instrucciones de aula (TPR) (RD 157/2022, primer ciclo de Educación Primaria).

  • Instrucciones con respuesta física total (Stand up, Sit down…).
  • Kim's game con material escolar.
  • Tienda de clase con diálogos de cortesía.
  • Etiquetar el aula en inglés con el alumnado.

Fuentes y revisión

  • Real Decreto 157/2022, enseñanzas mínimas de la Educación Primaria (BOE)

Revisado el 14 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name school objects: pencil, rubber, book, bag…
  • Name things in the classroom: table, chair, board
  • Ask and answer What's this? It's a…
  • Understand classroom instructions: sit down, stand up, listen
  • Ask for things politely: Can I have a pencil, please?

Palabras clave

pencil · rubber · book · bag · crayon · scissors · ruler · table · chair · board · What's this?

Tiempo

50 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
